items.title: 2.8.2 Classification of the elements of the periodic table

source_refs.note: Topic 2.8.2, printed pages 39-40: representative, transition and inner transition elements and the building-up order (Figure 2.16), with Quick Check 2.6 as the self-check.

blocks.text: The main-group or representative elements all have valence-shell configurations ns(a) np(b), with some choice of a and b: their outer s or p subshell is being filled. In the d block transition elements a d subshell is being filled, and in the f block transition elements, or inner transition elements, an f subshell. There is a definite pattern to the order of filling as we go through the elements, from which the building-up order can be written: in the first period the 1s subshell fills; in the second, 2s and then, across the period, 2p; in the third, 3s and 3p; in the fourth, 4s, then 3d, then 4p. In the sketch of the table the ns area, the np area, the (n - 1)d area and the (n - 2)f area are marked. The classification of the elements into metals, non-metals, representative and transition elements, periods, groups and blocks is based on electronic configuration and valence electrons, so the chemical properties of each category can be assessed from it.

blocks.alt: A periodic-table outline with one label per row of each block: s block in blue with 1s above groups 1 and 18 and rows 2s to 7s; d block in yellow with rows 3d, 4d, 5d and 6d; p block in green with rows 2p to 7p; f block in two separate rows 4f and 5f. Marks * and ** in group 3 of periods 6 and 7 point to the 4f and 5f rows.
